# Recurrence oracle disagreements

Generated by `packages/engine/scripts/recurrence-oracle/generate.ts`; edit the readings in that script, not here.

- Oracle A: python-dateutil 3.0.0, zoneinfo (time zones from Python zoneinfo).
- Oracle B: the Google Calendar emulator expander, prov-emu-gcal a950d20, read-only.
- Golden corpus: 143 cases where every oracle that supports the case agrees.

## Disputed cases (kept out of golden.json)

Each is in `disputed.json` with both answers; the module is tested against the side named here.

### ordinal-yearly-20th-monday

Rule `FREQ=YEARLY;BYDAY=20MO;COUNT=3`.

- A: 20260518T160000Z, 20270517T160000Z, 20280515T160000Z (3)
- B: none
- Corpus side: **A**. RFC 5545 §3.3.10: with FREQ=YEARLY and no BYMONTH, a BYDAY ordinal counts within the year ("+20MO ... the 20th Monday within the YEARLY rule"). Oracle B counts within DTSTART's month instead (documented in its header), so it finds no 20th Monday at all. The corpus takes A (the RFC).

### ordinal-yearly-last-sunday-june-start

Rule `FREQ=YEARLY;BYDAY=-1SU;COUNT=3`.

- A: 20261227T100000Z, 20271226T100000Z, 20281231T100000Z (3)
- B: 20260628T090000Z, 20270627T090000Z, 20280625T090000Z (3)
- Corpus side: **A**. YEARLY;BYDAY=-1SU without BYMONTH is the last Sunday of the year (late December). B reads the ordinal within DTSTART's month and returns the last Sunday of June each year. A also drops the June DTSTART because the rule does not produce it (see the DTSTART note below). The corpus takes A.

### setpos-weekly-last-of-week

Rule `FREQ=WEEKLY;BYDAY=MO,WE,FR;BYSETPOS=-1;COUNT=6`.

- A: 20260109T140000Z, 20260116T140000Z, 20260123T140000Z, 20260130T140000Z, 20260206T140000Z, 20260213T140000Z (6)
- B: 20260105T140000Z, 20260107T140000Z, 20260109T140000Z, 20260112T140000Z, 20260114T140000Z, 20260116T140000Z (6)
- Corpus side: **A**. RFC 5545 §3.3.10 lets BYSETPOS apply to any frequency ("within the set of recurrence instances" of each interval); WEEKLY;BYDAY=MO,WE,FR;BYSETPOS=-1 is the Friday of each week. B applies BYSETPOS only for MONTHLY and YEARLY and so keeps all three days. The corpus takes A.

### setpos-yearly-across-months

Rule `FREQ=YEARLY;BYMONTH=1,2;BYDAY=MO;BYSETPOS=1;COUNT=3`.

- A: 20260105T140000Z, 20270104T140000Z, 20280103T140000Z (3)
- B: 20260105T140000Z, 20260202T140000Z, 20270104T140000Z (3)
- Corpus side: **A**. For YEARLY, BYSETPOS selects within the whole year's set (here every Monday of January and February), so BYSETPOS=1 is the first Monday of January only. B applies BYSETPOS month by month and also keeps the first Monday of February. The corpus takes A.

### mday-yearly-no-bymonth

Rule `FREQ=YEARLY;BYMONTHDAY=15;COUNT=4`.

- A: 20260115T140000Z, 20260215T140000Z, 20260315T130000Z, 20260415T130000Z (4)
- B: 20260115T140000Z, 20270115T140000Z (2)
- Corpus side: **A**. RFC 5545 §3.3.10's table marks BYMONTHDAY as "Expand" for YEARLY: without BYMONTH, YEARLY;BYMONTHDAY=15 is the 15th of every month of the year. B only uses DTSTART's month. The corpus takes A.

## A note that is not a disagreement: DTSTART that does not match the rule

RFC 5545 §3.3.10 says DTSTART "always counts as the first occurrence" but also that a recurrence set whose DTSTART is not synchronised with the rule is undefined. Both oracles (and Google) drop a DTSTART the rule does not produce, and so does the module; the cases `unsynced-dtstart-*` pin that. A CalDAV server that keeps such a DTSTART would show one more occurrence; it is a round-2 question for CalDAV.

## Oracle A defects the fuzz found (the module follows RFC 5545)

The seeded fuzz (`calendar-recurrence-fuzz.test.ts`) compares the module with oracle A over ten years. In three places dateutil is wrong and the module is right; the fuzz steers around the first two and hand tests pin the module's answers. No golden or disputed case depends on them.

- **WEEKLY with BYSETPOS.** RFC 5545 §3.3.10 applies BYSETPOS to "the set of recurrence instances" of each interval, which for WEEKLY is the whole week from WKST. dateutil counts only the days of DTSTART's week from DTSTART on. `WEEKLY;BYDAY=FR,WE,SA;WKST=WE;BYSETPOS=1` from Sat 15 Aug 2026: dateutil says 15 Aug, the RFC (and the module) say 19 Aug, because position 1 of that week is Wed 12 Aug, before DTSTART.
- **BYWEEKNO near 1 January.** Week 1 is the first week with at least four days of the year (§3.3.10). dateutil sizes the previous year from the current one, so with `WKST=SU` it calls 1-2 Jan 2027 week 53, but 2026 has 52 weeks and they are week 52. The three BYWEEKNO golden cases avoid this and rest on oracle A alone.
- **A start given as an exact instant on a fall-back night.** RFC 5545 §3.3.5 picks the first of two equal wall readings only for a local time with TZID. A start given as an instant (Google's `start.dateTime` with an offset) is that instant: 09:30Z on 1 Nov 2026 in Los Angeles is the second 01:30, and Google's id for that instance ends `_20261101T093000Z`. Oracle A reads the instant back as a wall time and lands on the first 01:30, as the module did before the fix; later instances take the first reading in both.

## Cases only one oracle supports (kept in golden.json with that one oracle)

Oracle A only (oracle B refuses the rule part):

- la-byhour-fallback (B: Error: Unsupported RRULE part BYHOUR)
- a-only-yearly-byyearday (B: Error: Unsupported RRULE part BYYEARDAY)
- a-only-yearly-byweekno-20 (B: Error: Unsupported RRULE part BYWEEKNO)
- a-only-yearly-byweekno-1-wkst-su (B: Error: Unsupported RRULE part BYWEEKNO)
- a-only-yearly-byweekno-53 (B: Error: Unsupported RRULE part BYWEEKNO)
- a-only-daily-byhour-byminute (B: Error: Unsupported RRULE part BYHOUR)
- a-only-monthly-byhour-setpos (B: Error: Unsupported RRULE part BYHOUR)
- a-only-yearly-last-day-of-year (B: Error: Unsupported RRULE part BYYEARDAY)

Oracle B only (dateutil refuses an UNTIL whose form differs from DTSTART's; RFC 5545 says it MUST match, but Google writes such rules, so the module reads them leniently the same way B does):

- b-only-timed-until-date (A: ValueError: RRULE UNTIL values must be specified in UTC when DTSTART is timezone-aware)
- b-only-timed-until-floating (A: ValueError: RRULE UNTIL values must be specified in UTC when DTSTART is timezone-aware)

## Property sweep

600 seeded rules were generated inside oracle B's subset; the first 300 on which A and B agree over three years are in `property-b.json`.
No generated rule was dropped for a disagreement before the 300 were reached.
